name: MALI
lead: Mali is a huge country with no coast. The Niger River curves along the edge of the Sahara. Mud-brick mosques rise like sandcastles. Griots keep old tales alive with kora harps and talking drums.
geo: Two-thirds of Mali is Sahara Desert, where heat can top 45 °C. The Niger River floods farms every year and feeds millions with fish and rice.
The Sahel grassland crosses the south and turns green after rains. The Bandiagara Cliffs rise 500 m. The Dogon people have carved villages into them for nearly a thousand years.
animals: Hippos and Nile crocodiles rest on the banks of the Niger. African manatees glide through quiet backwaters.
Fennec foxes with huge ears live in the north. Rare West African giraffes wander near the Niger's inland delta.
culture: A griot is a musician, historian and storyteller in one. Griots play the kora, a 21-string harp-lute made from a gourd.
The Great Mosque of Djenné is the world's largest mud-brick building. The whole town replasters it after every rainy season.
history: Around 1300 CE the Mali Empire ruled land bigger than Western Europe. Emperor Mansa Musa may be the wealthiest person ever. In 1324 he made a pilgrimage with 12,000 servants and tonnes of gold.
Timbuktu became a great centre of learning with over 25,000 students. Mali became independent from France on 22 September 1960.
wows: The Great Mosque of Djenné has been replastered every year for over 800 years.
Mansa Musa's 1324 caravan had 60,000 people and about 18 tonnes of gold.
Mali holds over 700,000 ancient manuscripts, some in family homes.
The Niger Inland Delta floods into a wetland the size of Belgium.
Europeans once offered prizes to anyone who could reach Timbuktu and return.
Ali Farka Touré's guitar style helped shape American blues.
The Niger is Africa's third-longest river.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: A hump holds fat, not water. The fat gives energy on long trips.

myths.myth: Timbuktu is not a real place
myths.fact: It is a real city in Mali. At its peak it had about 180 Quranic schools.
